sentences.text: Today, we will talk about Madagascar.
Madagascar is a big island full of nature, animals, and adventure.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Madagascar?
Madagascar is in the Indian Ocean near the east coast of Africa.
It is the fourth largest island in the world.
It is close to Mozambique, Tanzania, and Mauritius.
What is the capital city of Madagascar?
The capital city is Antananarivo.
It is in the central highlands.
People also call it Tana.
It has markets, schools, and hills with houses.
Other cities include Tomasina, a big port city.
Ansirabe, with cool weather and hot springs.
Fianaransoa, a cultural center in the south.
How many people live in Madagascar?
About 30 million people live in Madagascar.
Most people live in villages or small towns.
There are many ethnic groups, but they all share Malagasy culture.
What language do people speak in Madagascar?
People speak Malagasy, the national language.
Many also speak French, which is used in schools and offices.
In tourist places, some people speak a little English.
What is the weather like in Madagascar?
Madagascar has a tropical climate, hot and rainy in the summer, November to April, cool and dry in the winter, May to October.
The east coast is very rainy, the south and west are drier and hotter.
What does Madagascar look like?
Madagascar has rain forests and dry forests, mountains and plateaus, beaches and coral reefs, rivers, lakes and rice fields.
The land is full of amazing plants and unique animals.
What animals live in Madagascar?
Madagascar has many animals found only on the island.
Limbers, small primates with big eyes, chameleons, color changing lizards, baobab trees, tall trees with thick trunks, fossa, a wild cat -like animal, strange frogs, birds and insects.
It is a great place for wildlife lovers.
What do people eat in Madagascar?
Food in Madagascar is simple, local and delicious.

People eat rice at every meal, meat, chicken, beef or zebu, a type of cattle, vegetables, beans and greens, bananas, mangoes and coconuts, popular dishes, romazava, meat and leafy greens and broth, ravi toto, pork with mashed cassava leaves, lassopi, vegetable soup, coba, a sweet banana and peanut cake wrapped in leaves.
What do people drink in Madagascar?
People drink water and tea, coffee, often sweet and with lots of milk.
Fresh fruit juice?
Adults may drink homemade rum or banana wine.
What is life like in Madagascar?
Life is often slow, traditional and family based.
People enjoy farming and working outside, spending time with family, going to church or community events, dancing and singing, walking to markets and talking to neighbors.
Many people live in simple houses made from wood or clay.
What are some holidays and traditions in Madagascar?
Independence Day, June 26.
Alahamadi Bee, Malagasy New Year.
Famadihana, The Turning of the Bones, a special family tradition.
Christmas and Easter, local festivals with music, food and dancing.
Music is very important.
People love drums, flutes and guitar.
Some fun facts about Madagascar.
Madagascar is home to over 100 species of lemurs.
Many plants and animals are found nowhere else.
The flag is red, white and green.
Vanilla comes from Madagascar.
It is one of the top producers.
People use zebu carts and wooden canoes in rural areas.
Now you know many things about Madagascar.
You know where it is, what people eat and what animals live there.
You learned about life, traditions and nature.
Well done!
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
